text:
alex: quick thought — can we split the console query surface into a "projection" service for precomputed panels + a "query" service for ad-hoc/fanout requests? wondering about RBAC implications and perf tradeoffs.

maria: splitting seems sensible for scaling. projections = stable schemas, cheap reads; ad-hoc = expensive. RBAC is the tricky bit though — we currently enforce at the query layer.

sam: fwiw, projection service can store row-level access tokens or pre-filtered views per role. downside: explosion of materialized views.

alex: yeah that's my worry — materialized views per-team could blow up cost. any middle ground?

maria: what about a hybrid: projections for common panels (dashboard tiles), ad-hoc queries still hit the query service and run server-side RBAC checks. projection service stores a small access index to validate requests without duplicating data.

jordan: +1 hybrid. we should also consider pushdown of RBAC predicates so ad-hoc service can forward minimal filters to the storage layer. avoids fetching large result sets then filtering.

sam: pushdown makes sense but requires consistent auth predicates across services. that's an interface contract we must define in the API between console and query layer (and documented in the proxy).

alex: agreed. need a spec: 1) RBAC predicate DSL (simple boolean expressions), 2) projection metadata (which panels are safe to serve cached), 3) expiry/TTL semantics.

maria: also add telemetry: token-level latency + miss rate (projection vs ad-hoc). helps tune thresholds for when to materialize a panel.

jordan: for rollout: canary projections enabled per-org. default to ad-hoc for orgs not opted in. migration plan: backfill top-50 most-used panels first.

sam: tests: unit for predicate compiler, integration for pushdown + policy enforcement, e2e for migration where onboarding toggles to projection. add synthetic load tests to measure cost delta.

alex: one more practical note — projection schema must be stable across releases. avoid breaking field names: use projection contract with a version header. example header: ```Projection-Version: v2```

maria: good call. also include a fallback: if projection returns 403 or stale, ad-hoc service can immediately compute the tile (fail-open to correct data but with logging).

jordan: logging + regression alerts if ad-hoc compute spikes for a specific panel — we should auto-suggest materialization in Optimize dashboard.

dev-bot: CI pipeline: projection-dsl-tests passed — build 432. deploy staged to canary by jenkins/prod-canary at 1854323000. :white_check_mark:

alex: ok next steps: maria to draft API contract for predicate DSL and projection metadata; sam to prototype pushdown to storage; jordan to own rollout plan + telemetry signals. I'll open an RFC doc and link it here. :+1:
